newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Public school teachers plan to boycott any Palace-backed plebiscite to push through with consitutional amendments. Some groups said they will resist, if needed, any orders from the Department of Education to perform their duties in plebiscites. (TODAY)
- For the good of the country, President Ramos vowed yesterday to block any move that would prolong his stay in power after 1998. (STAR)

- An earthquake measuring seven on the Richter scale hit the main southern island of Mindanao, triggering a fire that damaged a hospital building but there were no reports of casualties, officials said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The House committee on banks and financial intermediaries on Wednesday ordered the submission of investigation results on insider trading and price manipulations at the Philippine Stock Exchange to determine whether it was the cause for the series of resignation of officials, including its President Vitaliano Nanagas. (MALAYA)

- The management of Philippine Airlines is exploring talks with several Asian and U.S. carriers for the possible sale of the unsubscribed shares of the flag carrier's new capital hike. (CHRONICLE/INQUIRER)
- The Central Bank wants the national government to convert its 40 billion-peso special deposits into additional equity to support the bank's operations. (STAR/JOURNAL)
